tools.name: search_flights
tools.description: First step. Search flight offers for one route on one date; no authorization needed. Returns up to two options, each a quote valid for ten minutes: the cheapest fare and the fastest journey (one option carrying both labels when they coincide), with itinerary — flight numbers, airline, airports, local departure and arrival times, stops — and fare in minor units. Choose one; its id is the input to create_checkout.

departure_date.description: Departure date, ISO 8601 calendar date, in the future.

correlation_id.description: Optional. Any UUID v4 your client generates, lowercase, one per transaction; omit it and the seller mints one. Echoed into every ledger entry this call writes so the chains can be joined.

exercise.description: Optional. A test-vector id (R-06, F-08) stating that this call is an exercise. Copied into every ledger entry the call writes as facts.claimed_exercise, as your claim; it changes nothing about how the call is checked.

correlation_id.description: The buyer's, echoed; or minted by the seller when none was sent (evidence says which through the ledger).

request_id.description: The seller's id for this call. Cite it when reporting a problem.

id.description: The quote id; the input to create_checkout.

total.description: Fare in minor units of currency.

local_time.description: Local to the airport, no offset: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM.

quote_jws.description: The quote as a compact JWS (typ quote+jwt), signed by the instance key. Forward it unchanged; the mandate is bound to its hash.

quote_hash.description: SHA-256, lowercase hex, over the raw decoded payload octets of quote_jws. Recompute it; never trust it.

audit_hash.description: Hash of the ledger entry that recorded this quote.

quote.description: The first option, kept for callers written before options existed.

id.description: The quote id; the input to create_checkout.

total.description: Fare in minor units of currency.

local_time.description: Local to the airport, no offset: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM.

quote_jws.description: The quote as a compact JWS (typ quote+jwt), signed by the instance key. Forward it unchanged; the mandate is bound to its hash.

quote_hash.description: SHA-256, lowercase hex, over the raw decoded payload octets of quote_jws. Recompute it; never trust it.

audit_hash.description: Hash of the ledger entry that recorded this quote.

provider.description: Where the fare came from. "fixture" means the announced fallback.

fallback.description: Present only when the live source answered nothing and the fixture answered instead; provider then reads "fixture".

signer.description: Who signed the quote and the receipt: the instance key the domain vouches for. Fetch key_url, check the SVID against the bundle it names, and verify with the JWK whose kid equals this one.

audit_hash.description: The ledger chain head after this call.

tools.name: create_checkout
tools.description: Second step, after search_flights. quote_id is the id of one of its options (options[].id, q_ followed by a UUID), valid ten minutes; there is no fixed example, and an id search_flights did not mint is refused as quote_unavailable. Needs a bearer authorization (see the agent card's securitySchemes.bearer for where one comes from). Turns the quote into a payment intent and stops there: no ticket is issued. A PaymentIntent is created at Stripe in test mode and confirmed with a test card (pm_card_visa); it succeeds and captures. Test mode: no real card, no real money.

quote_id.description: The id of the chosen option returned by search_flights (options[].id, q_ followed by a UUID), sent within ten minutes of that call. No fixed example exists: run search_flights first.

quote_hash.description: Optional. The hash you computed over the quote_jws payload; the seller recomputes its own and refuses a mismatch.

merchant_id.description: This merchant. Any other value is refused.

currency.description: ISO 4217. This merchant quotes in one currency and refuses the rest.

correlation_id.description: Optional. Any UUID v4 your client generates, lowercase, one per transaction; omit it and the seller mints one. Echoed into every ledger entry this call writes so the chains can be joined.

mandate_jws.description: Required when the call is a signed request envelope (typ request+jwt): the cart-stage mandate from an authority this merchant trusts, typ mandate+jwt, bound to quote_hash and to the key that signed the envelope.

exercise.description: Optional. A test-vector id (R-06, F-08) stating that this call is an exercise. Copied into every ledger entry the call writes as facts.claimed_exercise, as your claim; it changes nothing about how the call is checked.

correlation_id.description: Optional. Any UUID v4 your client generates, lowercase, one per transaction; omit it and the seller mints one. Echoed into every ledger entry this call writes so the chains can be joined.

local_time.description: Local to the airport, no offset: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM.

payment_intent.description: In simulation the id starts with pi_sim_ and stays requires_payment_method; at Stripe test mode it is a real pi_ confirmed with a test card, reaching succeeded.

settlement.description: What happened to the money, as the checkout.completed ledger entry records it. charged is false on the simulation rail and true on stripe-test, where the capture is a test card in Stripe test mode (no real money).

outcome.description: simulated: no intent exists anywhere. intent_created: an intent exists at the rail and is not confirmed. captured: an intent was confirmed and captured (on stripe-test, a test card in the sandbox).

receipt_jws.description: Compact JWS (typ receipt+jwt) signed by the instance key, citing quote_hash, the payment intent and the ledger entry.

signer.description: Who signed the quote and the receipt: the instance key the domain vouches for. Fetch key_url, check the SVID against the bundle it names, and verify with the JWK whose kid equals this one.

audit_hash.description: The payment_intent.created entry, the one the receipt cites.

completion_hash.description: The checkout.completed entry: the end of this checkout in the ledger, citing the intent entry and the receipt.
